hints: Focus on what an oxidising agent actually does, it gets reduced itself while it oxidises the other species.
Notice hydrogen starts as $\text{H}_2$ with oxidation number 0 in every equation, so check what it becomes in the products.
Look for the one equation where hydrogen gains electrons and its oxidation number falls from 0 to -1.
walkthrough:
**Recall what an oxidising agent is**

An oxidising agent oxidises someone else, so it is itself reduced. Reduced means gain of electrons, and fall in oxidation number.

Rule to use:
$$\text{oxidising agent is reduced : oxidation number decreases}$$

**Track the oxidation number of hydrogen**

In $\text{H}_2$, hydrogen is an uncombined element, so its oxidation number is 0. Now check the products.

$$\text{H}_2 (0) \to \text{H}^{+1} \text{ means oxidised, } \text{H}_2 (0) \to \text{H}^{-1} \text{ means reduced}$$

**Apply to the four equations**

In B, C and D hydrogen ends up as $\text{HI}$, $\text{H}_2\text{O}$ and $\text{NH}_3$, all containing $\text{H}^{+1}$. That is an increase from 0 to +1, so hydrogen is oxidised and acts as a reducing agent. Only in one equation does hydrogen go from 0 to $\text{H}^{-}$ in the hydride ion, a decrease, so hydrogen is reduced and acts as the oxidising agent.

options.A: In $\text{H}_2 + 2\text{K} \to 2\text{K}^{+}\text{H}^{-}$, hydrogen changes from 0 in $\text{H}_2$ to -1 in $\text{H}^{-}$. It gains electrons and is reduced, while potassium is oxidised from 0 to +1. A reduced species is the oxidising agent, so this is correct.
options.B: In $\text{H}_2 + \text{I}_2 \to 2\text{HI}$, hydrogen changes from 0 to +1 in $\text{HI}$. It loses electrons and is oxidised, so hydrogen is acting as a reducing agent, not an oxidising agent.
options.C: In $\text{H}_2 + \text{Cu}_2\text{S} + \text{ZnO} \to 2\text{Cu} + \text{ZnS} + \text{H}_2\text{O}$, hydrogen changes from 0 to +1 in $\text{H}_2\text{O}$. It is oxidised, so it is the reducing agent. Students sometimes get distracted by copper being reduced from +1 to 0, but the question asks about hydrogen.
options.D: In $3\text{H}_2 + \text{N}_2 \to 2\text{NH}_3$, hydrogen changes from 0 to +1 in $\text{NH}_3$ while nitrogen is reduced from 0 to -3. Hydrogen is oxidised, so it is the reducing agent here.
